headline: MANY PEAKS MINERALS HITS 46.75m AT 7.02g/t GOLD AT OUARIGUE — 1.85m AT 109.8g/t BONANZA CORE CONFIRMS DEPTH POTENTIAL
snippet: Many Peaks Minerals (ASX: MPK) reported October 13 that drill hole FNDC166 at its Ouarigue gold project intersected 46.75m at 7.02g/t gold from 775.2m depth, including a high-grade core of 1.85m at 109.8g/t gold. The result extends the deposit's high-grade footprint at depth, demonstrating that the gold system remains open below current resource boundaries and strengthening the case for a larger resource estimate.

headline: BHP ESCONDIDA SUPERVISORS WALK OUT — WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINE ON STRIKE AS CHILE'S TRIPLE DISRUPTION SENDS LME COPPER TO 2-WEEK HIGH
snippet: Supervisors at BHP's Escondida mine — the world's largest copper mine at over 1 million tonnes per year — have gone on strike after government mediation failed to resolve a contract dispute. The walkout escalates Chile's copper supply crisis: El Teniente was partially suspended after a deadly avalanche, Centinela supervisors are on hunger strike in Santiago, and now Escondida faces a work stoppage. LME copper climbed to a two-week high above $14,600 per tonne on the compounding supply risk, with BMO analysts projecting output impacts could materialize in November.

headline: ASTRAL RESOURCES DRILLS 33m AT 5.02g/t BELOW KALGOORLIE'S THEIA PIT — HIGH-GRADE DEPTH EXTENSION OPENS UNDERGROUND MINE CASE
snippet: Astral Resources (ASX: AAR) announced October 13 that its Theia Deeps program at the Mandilla project near Kalgoorlie returned 33m at 5.02g/t gold beneath the designed open pit boundary. Management flagged the result as supporting a potential underground mine scenario below the Theia pit shell, adding a second development pathway to what was previously framed as a standalone open pit project.

headline: PC GOLD BUSTS OUTSIDE 1.51Moz SPRING HILL RESOURCE: NEW NORTH LINK ZONE RETURNS 2m AT 10.03g/t
snippet: PC Gold (ASX: PC2) disclosed October 13 RC drilling results that defined a new North Link zone entirely outside its existing 1.51 million ounce Spring Hill resource boundary, with best intercepts of 2m at 10.03g/t gold and 3m at 7.94g/t gold. Ten additional holes remain unreported; continued success in the North Link zone could add materially to the resource and strengthen Spring Hill's development case.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,165 AS DOLLAR FIRMS AHEAD OF TOMORROW'S CPI — METALS COMPLEX IN WAIT-AND-SEE MODE
snippet: Gold eased to approximately $4,165 per ounce on October 13 as a firm US dollar kept buyers cautious ahead of the October 14 Consumer Price Index release — the first major inflation test before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. Silver held near $60.50 with the gold-silver ratio at 68.8. A below-consensus CPI print could revive momentum toward January's $5,589 all-time high; a hotter-than-expected number risks sending gold back toward the $4,000 support zone.

headline: WILL TOMORROW'S CPI BREAK GOLD OUT OR KNOCK IT BACK? ANALYSTS LAY OUT THE TWO-WAY METALS SETUP FOR THIS WEEK
snippet: FXEmpire's October 13 technical analysis maps out a binary outcome from Wednesday's US CPI: a soft print could push gold decisively above $4,200 resistance and send silver toward $65, while a hotter-than-expected number risks a 3-4% pullback as rate-cut probability gets repriced. The analysis frames gold's consolidation above $4,100 as technically constructive, noting that record ETF holdings of 4,256 tonnes signal structural buyers will use any CPI-driven dip as an accumulation opportunity rather than a trend reversal.

headline: RARE EARTH ROUT: USARE AND MP MATERIALS EACH DROP 6% ON OCT. 12 — GOVERNMENT MILESTONE FUNDING STILL UNCOLLECTED AS SECTOR BLEEDS
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USARE) and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) each fell roughly 6% on October 12 as the rare earth sector sold off at nearly five times the pace of the broader market. For USARE, government reimbursements remain uncollected and tied to production milestones not yet achieved under new CEO Thras Moraitis, who took over October 1. Critical Metals (NASDAQ: CRML) — which recently secured its Greenland mining licence through 2050 — held relatively steady. The VanEck REMX ETF dropped 5% on the session.

headline: GREENLAND MINES SURGES 21% ON US-GREENLAND SECURITY DEAL — $12M SHARE RAISE TESTS WHETHER THE RARE EARTH RUN CAN HOLD
snippet: Greenland Mines Corp (NASDAQ: GRML) jumped 21.05% to USD 6.26 as investors drove up the stock on rare earth and geopolitical tailwinds following the US-Denmark-Greenland security framework signed September 22. The rally came alongside a USD 12 million equity raise to fund project development, creating a dilution overhang that Kalkine's analysis frames as the key near-term test of whether institutional buyers will step in to defend the gains or let them fade.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM PRICE CLIMBS TO $97/LB AS GRID GROWTH AND AI DATA CENTERS ACCELERATE NUCLEAR DEMAND — 18-YEAR HIGH
snippet: Long-term uranium contract prices have reached $97 per pound — an 18-year high — as electricity demand growth from AI data centers and grid expansion accelerates the timeline for new nuclear capacity. The indicator price crossed the 2007 record of $95/lb in late September and has continued higher, driven by a wave of utility re-contracting. For uranium developers and royalty companies, the price signal validates the bull thesis, though equity valuations continue to lag the commodity as investors wait for a visible wave of multi-year utility supply contracts to confirm sustained structural demand.
